title: Helping Lizzie Miles's comeback
summary: Mares promoted Miles on his radio show, got her a club job and a record date, and ended up helping Pete Fountain too.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: I understand that you helped Lizzie Miles with her comeback too.

Yes, I did, Bill. Well, Lizzie had been retired about 13 years. And she was working a little spot, wasn't doing too good. And Lizzie was dying to make a comeback. She rode a couple of disc jockeys here, didn't pay any attention to her. Well, I had a little radio program of my own for four and a half years, plugging Dixieland at WSMB. And I also took a little time on Tony Almerickas. Tony at that time was ill. So I went on for him for two weeks. In the meantime, I had the Johnny Saint-Cien, Paul Barber, George Lewis, and all the big names as guests. So one Friday afternoon, I got in touch with Lizzie and I asked her to come on up. I want to interview her on the air. I brought her up there and I said, Lizzie, how's your voice? She says, well, after 13 years, she said, I think it's more powerful today than it was in the early 20s. So I said, well, all right, I'm going to try you out Sunday evening. So I brought her to a concert and let Lizzie sing a couple of tunes. She brought the house down. So I walked over that evening and I, to a friend of mine, Steve Villani, who has the Paddock Club on Boydman Street, and I said, Steve, put Lizzie Miles to work. I must say so. And that's, she came back. I made a record date with her on my Southland. I got her a capital contract and I brought Lizzie into Linfen's Lounge to play the concerts with Shockey and so forth. And I think I've done a little bit to help Lizzie. Yeah, I'm sure. I've heard of that before. And while we're talking about helping some different musicians, I was very, very glad to help little Pete Fountain. Pete wasn't doing too much around here.
